# IKControl

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("IKControl")`

Bends a limb to reach a place, or turns a head to look at one, on top of whatever clip is playing (ADR 0198): a hand set on a weapon's grip, a foot put on a pedal, eyes that follow what walks past. Parent it to the `MeshPart` whose skeleton it bends, name the joint at the END of the limb -- the hand, the foot, the head -- and give it a `Target`.

**It is picture, not simulation.** It is solved on each machine, each frame, into the pose the frame is drawn with, and never into the pose the tick reads: a `Bone` on that hand still says where the clip has the hand, and nothing in the game's rules should read a reached-for place. What a script turns for the rules to see -- a head whose turn decides what a guard notices -- it turns with `Bone.Transform`. What IS drawn follows: a part held to a bone of the limb is drawn in the hand that was moved, and a cape hangs from shoulders an arm's reach moved.

It reaches as far as the limb is long and stops there, straight. In a match the control and what it is set to travel with its character; the bending is each machine's own.

**Members below are the ones this class DECLARES.** Everything its base
offers is on the base's page, which is what keeps one added member on
`Instance` from being a change to every page here.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AlignRotation` | `boolean` | — | read/write | For a limb: whether the end takes the target's turn as well as its place -- a palm laid flat on a grip, a sole on a pedal. |
| `ChainLength` | `number` | `2` | read/write | For a look: how many joints above the end share the turn, 0 to 8 -- a head alone, a head and its neck, a head, a neck and a spine. Each takes an equal part. |
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether it is applied at all. Off costs nothing. |
| `EndJoint` | `string` | — | read/write | The joint at the end of what is bent, as the file names it: a hand, a foot, a head. A name the rig does not have does nothing. |
| `MaxAngle` | `number` | `70` | read/write | For a look: the furthest from straight ahead it may turn, in degrees. Past it the look stops at the limit instead of twisting the neck round. |
| `Pole` | `(BasePart | Attachment)?` | — | read/write | For a limb: what the elbow or the knee points at. With none the limb bends the way the clip already has it bent. |
| `Smoothing` | `number` | `0.1` | read/write | The seconds a change is eased over -- a target that jumps, a control switched on -- so a head turns to a new thing instead of snapping to it. 0 follows at once. |
| `Target` | `(BasePart | Attachment)?` | — | read/write | What is reached for or looked at: a part or an attachment, where it is DRAWN this frame. With none the control does nothing. |
| `TargetOffset` | `CFrame` | — | read/write | Where from the target the place is, in the target's own space: a grip a hand's width from a weapon's middle. |
| `Type` | `Enum.IKControlType` | `Enum.IKControlType.TwoBone` | read/write | `TwoBone`: the end joint, the one above it and the one above that are a limb, and the end is put at the target. `LookAt`: the end joint is turned to face the target, and the joints above it share the turn. |
| `Weight` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How much of it is applied, 0 to 1: 0 is the clip alone. Tween it to pick a thing up and let it go without a snap. |
